subject: Benchmark acceptance: latency & throughput telemetry exchange for CloudCart
messages:
From: Claire Nguyen <claire@cloudcart.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Tom Alvarez <tom.alvarez@cloudcart.com>, infra@cloudcart.com
Date: Sat, 18 Oct 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Benchmark run and acceptance criteria (CloudCart)

Hi Mina / Laura,

Thanks for the onboarding kickoff last week. To keep momentum we'd like to lock down the acceptance artifacts and schedule a short window to run a full throughput / latency verification against our production-ish load profile. High-level asks from CloudCart: 

- Target sustained throughput: 500 req/s (95th percentile at typical 1k token prompts)
- Acceptable p95 latency: <= 200ms per token generation (end-to-end request)
- Target 99th tail: ideally < 450ms; >450ms will need mitigation plan
- Test duration: 30 minute steady-state + 10 minute ramp/soak

Can you confirm what evidence you need from our side (telemetry schema, sample traces, load driver config) and what Redwood will provide (token-level breakdown, KV cache hit rates, model variant used, bench harness logs)? Attached is our initial load profile (cloudcart_loadplan_v1.xlsx).

We'd like to schedule a run for next Tuesday (10/21) morning PST if that works. Please advise next steps and who from your side will be present on the run.

Thanks,
Claire Nguyen
Head of SRE, CloudCart
claire@cloudcart.com

--
Attachment: cloudcart_loadplan_v1.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)

From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwoodinference.com>
To: Claire Nguyen <claire@cloudcart.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sat, 18 Oct 2025 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Benchmark run and acceptance criteria (CloudCart)

Claire — thanks for the clear asks and for the load profile. Confirming we're aligned on evidence and cadence. Proposed plan (high level):

1) Smoke (15m): quick sanity to validate routing, model variant, and basic perf counters.
2) Ramp to target (10m): step from 50 -> 500 req/s in 6 steps, observe tail and queueing.
3) Sustained steady-state (30m): collect full telemetry — traces, token-level timing, KV cache metrics, GPU utilization, batching stats.
4) Soak & clean: 10m soak followed by artifact collection and trace export.

Acceptance criteria (proposed, based on your targets):
- Sustained throughput >= 490 req/s for a 30m window
- p95 end-to-end latency <= 200ms
- p99 end-to-end latency <= 450ms (soft pass: up to 500ms with a mitigation plan)

Artifacts Redwood will produce and share after the run:
- latency_results_20251020.csv (per-request timings and percentiles)
- aggregated token breakdown (token gen ms/token)
- KV cache hit-rate logs and batch size distribution
- model variant + commit hash used for the run

We can host the run on Tuesday 10/21 09:00-10:30 PST (we'll reserve capacity). Ben and Monica will own telemetry collection and post-run artifact packaging. If CloudCart infra wants specific exporters, please send them this week.

Next steps: 
- Claire: confirm the window and if infra@cloudcart.com will add any extra synthetic agents.
- Tom: share the load-driver config you plan to run (we can run it from your JMeter k6 scripts or run Redwood's harness).

Thanks — we'll put together a checklist and share the runbook link.

—
Mina Haddad
Senior Product Manager, Onboarding
Redwood Inference
mina_haddad@redwoodinference.com

--
Quoted attachment: cloudcart_loadplan_v1.xlsx

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Claire Nguyen <claire@cloudcart.com>, Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sun, 19 Oct 2025 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Benchmark run and acceptance criteria (CloudCart)

Adding a few operational details so expectations are crystal: 

Telemetry & logs we will collect (and what we need from CloudCart):
- Per-request timing (client-sent -> first-byte -> last-byte) — Redwood will provide CSV.
- Token generation timing: ms/token and distribution by position (we'll include this in token breakdown).
- KV cache hit/miss rates (critical if you use long sessions) — please confirm whether cache is warmed with representative prefixes.
- Batch size distribution and queue depth histograms.
- GPU-side counters: SM utilization, memory, and quantized kernel metrics (Redwood will include summaries).

For reproducibility, please include (from CloudCart):
- load-driver command & seed/seed lists, concurrency profile, and any think-time configs
- exact prompt templates (or sanitized replicas) used for the run

Runbook & artifact dropbox: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b-cloudcart-benchmarks — after the run we will upload latency_results_20251020.csv and a README with interpretation notes.

If we see p99 drift > 450ms, we'll do a quick A/B to try: 1) increase soft-batch target; 2) enable prefix-level KV caching for warm sessions; 3) switch to an alternate model quantization profile. We'll capture all A/B variants as separate artifacts.

> Claire — thanks for the clear asks and for the load profile..."

Ben Carter

From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwoodinference.com>
To: Claire Nguyen <claire@cloudcart.com>, Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 20 Oct 2025 16:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Benchmark run and acceptance criteria (CloudCart) — run results and next steps

Claire / Team — thanks for running with us today. Summary of the outcome and artifacts (attached / uploaded):

What we ran
- Harness: Redwood's distributed load harness (k6-based) with your prompt corpus (sanitized).
- Model variant: rwinf-opt-3b-quant (commit: d41f3b2)
- Window: 2025-10-20 09:05 — 09:55 PST (30m steady-state)

High level results
- Sustained throughput: 512 req/s (measured over 30m) — PASS
- p95 end-to-end latency: 182ms — PASS
- p99 end-to-end latency: 489ms — SOFT FAIL (target <= 450ms)

Notes on p99
- Tail spikes correlated with short bursts of large-batch composition from a small subset of sessions (2% of traffic) where prompts averaged 1.8x token length.
- KV cache hit-rate overall 84%; sessions with cold prefixes had p99 ~ 720ms.
- GPU traces show occasional jitter aligned to background GC in the orchestration host (we've flagged infra).

Artifacts produced
- latency_results_20251020.csv (per-request timing with tags) — attached
- tail-99-screenshot.png — a plot of the 99th latency over the run — attached
- Token breakdown CSV and KV cache export — uploaded to: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b-cloudcart-benchmarks
- Run README with recommended mitigations — uploaded

Recommended next steps
1) Short-term: enable prefix-level warm caching for known long sessions & increase per-worker soft-batch target to reduce queue churn. We can schedule a targeted A/B tomorrow and iterate quickly.
2) Medium-term: add an agent-side pacing rule to avoid microbursts from client-side retries.
3) Infra: CloudCart infra to review orchestration host GC schedule — we can re-run with dedicated hosts if needed.

Acceptance guidance
- Given throughput and p95 pass, and p99 within a reasonable mitigation path, Redwood recommends a conditional acceptance: CloudCart marks this run as "accepted with mitigations" and we treat the outstanding p99 as a post-accept action with a 2-week remediation target.

Can you confirm CloudCart's preference: 1) Accept with mitigations and proceed to limited rollout, or 2) require a hard p99 <= 450ms before any rollout? Once you confirm we'll create a short remediation plan and timeline.

Thanks all — packaged artifacts attached.

—
Monica Patel
Implementation Lead, Customer Success
Redwood Inference
monica_patel@redwoodinference.com
